title: Bridging Number-Theoretic Primality Testing And Algorithmic Optimization: An Adaptive Cryptographic Framework
abstract: arXiv:2610.30935v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The security of modern public-key cryptographic systems, such as RSA, Diffie-Hellman, and ECC, depends entirely on the computational intractability of the integer factorization and discrete logarithm problems. For these asymmetric algorithms to operate, a core requirement is that the system must be capable of generating, testing, and simultaneously proving the primality of extraordinarily large numbers. To meet those requirements, this study proposes a comprehensive framework, bridging clas- sical number theory with modern machine learning models and optimization algorithms. Specifically, the paper delineates an adaptive, arbitrary-precision architecture dedicated exclusively to primality testing. translated_title: 桥接数论素性检测与算法优化：一种自适应密码学框架
translated_abstract: 现代公钥密码系统（如RSA、Diffie-Hellman和ECC）的安全性完全依赖于整数分解问题和离散对数问题的计算难解性。这些非对称算法要正常运行，一个核心要求是系统必须能够生成、检测并同时证明超大数字的素性。为满足这些需求，本研究提出了一个综合性框架，将经典数论与现代机器学习模型及优化算法相桥接。具体而言，本文设计了一种专门用于素性检测的自适应、任意精度架构。与此同时，该研究深入分析了检测方法（包括确定性方法和概率性方法）的理论基础、硬件级优化技术以及量子安全熵源的应用，并提供了……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个将经典数论与机器学习模型及优化算法相结合的自适应任意精度素性检测框架，以满足RSA等公钥密码系统对大素数生成、检测与证明的核心需求。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a comprehensive adaptive framework that bridges classical number theory with modern machine learning models and optimization algorithms for arbitrary-precision primality testing, meeting the core cryptographic requirements of generating, testing, and proving the primality of extraordinarily large numbers in systems such as RSA, Diffie-Hellman, and ECC.
